title: Finite-rank error after adjusting a coefficient section
statement: Let $k\subseteq K$ be fields of characteristic $p>0$ [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative local $k$-algebra, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $r:\Lambda\to K$ be a ring map compatible with the $k$-structures and with kernel $\mathfrak m$. Fix a finite subset $t\subset\Lambda$ spanning $\mathfrak m$ as an ideal. Let $I\subseteq\mathfrak m$ be an ideal with $\mathfrak mI=0$. Let $\sigma_0:K\to\Lambda$ be a section of $r$ and $c_0\subset K$ a finite subset. Let $\psi:k\to\Lambda$ be a ring map equal to the structure map $i$ modulo $I$, whose values lie in $\operatorname{Subring.closure}(t\cup\sigma_0(k(c_0)))$. Assume $H_1(L_{K/k})$ is finite dimensional over $K$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then there exist a section $\sigma:K\to\Lambda$ of $r$, unchanged from $\sigma_0$ modulo $I$, and a finite subset $f\subset I$, such that for each $a\in k$ there is $b\in\operatorname{Subring.closure}(t\cup\sigma(k(c_0)))$ with $i(a)-b\in\operatorname{span}_k(f)$. Here derivations and their universal modules are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and span uses the given $k$-algebra action on $\Lambda$.

source.place: Tag 07FG, proof of the coefficient-field claim (read at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07FG)

proof.text: Let theta be the additive difference of the structure map and psi. Quotient equality puts all its values in I. Because I is contained in ker r and (ker r)I=0, the product of two discrepancy values is zero. Expanding this identity gives the Leibniz rule for theta; theta(1)=0 follows from the ring-map identities.

Apply the finite-rank defect derivation theorem to theta. It gives an additive D:K to Lambda with sigma0-Leibniz rule, D(1)=0 and image in I, and a finite family f in I with theta(a)-D(algebraMap k K a) in span_k(f). The hypotheses (ker r)I=0 and residue compatibility follow directly from the given maximal-ideal identity and hcomm.

Construct the ring endomorphism beta(x)=x+D(r(x)). For multiplication, sigma0(r(x))-x lies in ker r and annihilates D(r(y)); the product of two D-values also vanishes. These identities and Leibniz prove multiplicativity by expansion. Set sigma=beta composed with sigma0. Since r(D(x))=0, it is a section; since D(x) lies in I, it has the same reduction as sigma0.

For each generator t, r(t)=0, so beta fixes t. It sends sigma0(y) to sigma(y). The universal property of subring closure therefore puts beta(psi(a)) in the corrected coefficient closure. The discrepancy theta(a) belongs to ker r, so r(psi(a))=algebraMap k K a. Thus i(a)-beta(psi(a)) equals theta(a)-D(algebraMap k K a), which belongs to span_k(f) by the finite-rank lemma. This handles all ring expressions, including integer constants, through the single constructed endomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Tag 07FG, the finite discrepancy derivation argument. Lean supplies the discrepancy calculation and the ring endomorphism beta(x)=x+D(r(x)); differential-basis steps are isolated in the generic finite-rank defect derivation theorem.
